-- UIParent.lua l.14-42: UIPanelWindows["FrameName"] = { area, pushable, whileDead }. Only the -- rows benilla ships/anticipates today (pin §1): Gossip + Merchant are live; Loot registers -- now (pushable=7) so the coming loot window lands on an already-wired system. UIPanelWindows = {} UIPanelWindows["BenillaGossipFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["BenillaMerchantFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The mail window (decision 0544): the reference UIParent.lua l.37 registers MailFrame -- area="left", pushable=0. The OpenMailFrame is NOT a panel — it is a special-frame toplevel -- (UIParent.lua l.46 UISpecialFrames), closed by ESC in BenillaOnEscape below (this v1 drops -- the UISpecialFrames table, so escapable toplevels are hard-listed there, like WorldMapFrame). UIPanelWindows["BenillaMailFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The trade window (decision 0592 P1, TradeFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.27 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["TradeFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 1 }`). Without -- this row ShowUIPanel takes its unregistered branch — a bare frame:Show() with no left-slot -- placement — so the window flips IsShown() but never lands on screen (the bug: OPEN_WINDOW -- arrived on both clients, yet no window). pushable=1 lets a pushable=0 panel (a merchant) -- shove it to center, the reference's browse-while-trading arbitration. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTradeFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 1 } -- The trainer window (decision 0237 phase 3, TrainerFrame.xml): an NPC session exactly like -- Gossip/Merchant above (area "left", pushable 0) — competes for/replaces them at the slot. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTrainerFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The bank window (decision 0604 phase 4, BankFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.28 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["BankFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 }`), quoted -- verbatim — the same left-slot competition as the other NPC-session windows above. UIPanelWindows["BenillaBankFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 } -- The taxi-map window (decision 0484 phase 2, TaxiFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua -- registration line (`UIPanelWindows["TaxiFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 }`), -- quoted verbatim — same left-slot competition as Gossip/Merchant/Trainer above. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTaxiFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["BenillaQuestFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["BenillaQuestLogFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["BenillaLootFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 7 } -- The character window (decision 0208 phase 1a, CharacterFrame.xml): the ref's own -- CharacterFrame row (area "left", pushable 0) — competes for/replaces the other left-slot -- windows exactly like Gossip/Merchant/Quest/QuestLog above. UIPanelWindows["BenillaCharacterFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The spellbook (decision 0216 §8, SpellBookFrame.xml): the ref's own SpellBookFrame row -- (area "left", pushable 0) — same left-slot competition as every window above. UIPanelWindows["BenillaSpellBookFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The talent window (decision 0304 §4, TalentFrame.xml): the ref's own TalentFrame row is -- `{ area = "left", pushable = 6, whileDead = 1 }` — pushable 6 kept (one tier above the -- plain NPC-session/player-state windows' 0, matching the ref exactly); `whileDead` is -- OMITTED like every other row here (none of them model it, even though ShowUIPanel's own -- guard already reads `info.whileDead` — ShowUIPanel's own comment: `UnitIsDead` doesn't -- exist yet, so the guard is inert either way today). UIPanelWindows["BenillaTalentFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 } -- The crafting window (decision 0437 phase 2, TradeSkillFrame.xml): NOT an NPC session (it -- opens off your own cast, TradeSkillFrame.xml's own header comment) — the ref Lua's own -- registration line (Blizzard_TradeSkillUI.lua:13) is `{ area = "left", pushable = 3 }`, -- quoted verbatim. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTradeSkillFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 3 } -- The Enchanting window (decision 0437 phase 3, CraftFrame.xml): the ref Lua's own -- registration line (`Blizzard_CraftUI.lua:24`), quoted verbatim — `pushable = 4`, NOT `3` -- (grepped both ref files directly to confirm: `3` is TradeSkillFrame's own line-13 value, -- a different window/depth — CraftFrame.xml's own header comment has the same note). UIPanelWindows["BenillaCraftFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 4 }
-- The real client stores `.left`/`.center`/`.doublewide`/`.fullscreen` as fields directly on -- the `UIParent` frame table (UIParent.lua l.789-885). benilla has no `UIParent` frame object -- yet (a later decision's job) — so the two slots this v1 tracks live in a private chunk-local -- table instead of squatting the `UIParent` global name; a future `CreateFrame("Frame", -- "UIParent")` then lands cleanly on an empty global rather than silently coexisting with our -- state. Every function below is defined in this same chunk, so they all close over it. local slots = { left = nil, center = nil }
-- SetLeftFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.809-824. Hides the old left occupant, SetPoints + -- Shows the new one at the left slot's screen anchor (verified: TOPLEFT UIParent, 0, -104). -- "UIParent" as the relativeTo name doesn't resolve to a real frame yet (none exists) — the -- engine's SetPoint falls back to the frame's own parent-or-screen default, which for our -- top-level panel frames IS the screen root, so this already anchors correctly; the string is -- kept for fidelity/forward-compat with the day a real UIParent frame lands. function SetLeftFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.left slots.left = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) frame:Show() end end
-- SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) — UIParent.lua l.826-850. The `UIChildWindows` hide loop -- (l.840-846) is dropped: no such frames exist in benilla yet (out of v1 scope). function SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) local oldFrame = slots.center slots.center = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:Show() if not skipSetPoint then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) end end end
-- MovePanelToLeft() — UIParent.lua l.868-875: the center occupant slides back to the left slot -- (used when the left slot vacates and a "left-area" frame is holding center). function MovePanelToLeft() if slots.center then SetLeftFrame(nil) slots.center:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) slots.left = slots.center slots.center = nil end end
-- MovePanelToCenter() — UIParent.lua l.877-885: the left occupant slides to the center slot -- (used when a higher-`pushable` frame wants the left spot). `:Raise()` (l.881) has no benilla -- frame-level equivalent yet — guarded, same posture as the pin's `UnitIsDead` guard below. function MovePanelToCenter() if slots.left then SetCenterFrame(nil) slots.left:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) if slots.left.Raise then slots.left:Raise() end slots.center = slots.left slots.left = nil end end
-- GetLeftFrame / GetCenterFrame — UIParent.lua l.916-922. function GetLeftFrame() return slots.left end
function GetCenterFrame() return slots.center end
-- ShowUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.649-751, v1 left+center slice only (pin §3 steps 1,3-5). -- Skipped by scope: `CanOpenPanels()` (l.655 — no gate exists to open panels on yet), -- full-screen (l.668-675) and native-center (l.677-689) precedence (no `full`/`center`-area -- panel ships), and the `full`/`doublewide` branches (l.692-710 — no such row is registered). function ShowUIPanel(frame, force) if not frame or frame:IsVisible() then return end
local info = UIPanelWindows[frame:GetName()] if not info then frame:Show() return end
-- UnitIsDead doesn't exist yet (pin §3) — guarded rather than assumed absent-forever. if type(UnitIsDead) == "function" and UnitIsDead("player") and not info.whileDead then return end
if info.area ~= "left" then -- No center/full/doublewide row is registered in v1 — defensive fallback only. frame:Show() return end
-- Try to put it on the left (l.719-723). local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame() if not leftFrame then SetLeftFrame(frame) return end
local leftInfo = UIPanelWindows[leftFrame:GetName()] local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if not centerFrame then -- If neither is pushable, replace (l.729-732 — the gossip<->merchant case). if leftInfo.pushable == 0 and info.pushable == 0 then SetLeftFrame(frame) return end -- Highest priority goes to center (l.735-741). if leftInfo.pushable > info.pushable then MovePanelToCenter() SetLeftFrame(frame) else SetCenterFrame(frame) end return end
-- Center is already taken too (l.744-751). local centerInfo = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if info.pushable > centerInfo.pushable then MovePanelToLeft() SetCenterFrame(frame) else SetLeftFrame(frame) end end
-- HideUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.754-786, v1 left+center slice (the real fn's -- full-screen branch, l.759-763, is dropped: no full-screen row ships). function HideUIPanel(frame) if not frame or not frame:IsShown() then return end
if frame == GetCenterFrame() then SetCenterFrame(nil) return end
if frame == GetLeftFrame() then local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if centerFrame then local info = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if info and info.area == "left" then MovePanelToLeft() return end end SetLeftFrame(nil) return end
frame:Hide() end
-- CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) — UIParent.lua l.928-957, v1 left+center slice (the -- doublewide/full-screen/UISpecialFrames handling, l.932-954, is dropped: none exist yet). -- Implemented per the pin so the function exists; wiring it to ESC is a later slice. function CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame() local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() local found = leftFrame or centerFrame
HideUIPanel(leftFrame) if centerFrame then local info = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if not info or info.area ~= "center" or not ignoreCenter then HideUIPanel(centerFrame) end end
return found end
-- CloseAllWindows(ignoreCenter) — UIParent.lua l.970-982. The real fn first loops -- ContainerFrame1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES to hide any open bags, then calls CloseWindows() for -- the panel slots, returning whether anything closed. benilla ships a single backpack window -- (BenillaBagFrame, decision 0068 T2), so that loop collapses to hiding it. The bag is NOT a -- UIPanel (no slot registration) — it must be closed here explicitly, exactly as the real -- client closes its ContainerFrames outside the slot system. Naming BenillaBagFrame here -- mirrors UIParent.lua naming ContainerFrame in the very same function. function CloseAllWindows(ignoreCenter) local bagsVisible = nil -- Hide every open bag window — the backpack plus the four equipped-bag windows (the real -- fn's ContainerFrame1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES loop). Now that 'B' opens all bags at once -- (BagFrame.xml BenillaBagToggle_OnClick), ESC must close all of them, not just the -- backpack. The list is inlined (not BagFrame.xml's BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS) so this stays -- nil-safe on a surface without the bag file — a headless panel test — per window. local bags = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4" } for _, name in ipairs(bags) do local bag = getglobal(name) if bag and bag:IsShown() then bag:Hide() bagsVisible = 1 end end local windowsVisible = CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) return bagsVisible or windowsVisible end
-- OpenBackpack / CloseBackpack — the real ContainerFrame.lua globals (l.187-217) the -- vendor/bank/mail/trade windows call from their OnShow/OnHide so your bags open with them -- (playing igBackPackOpen/Close alongside the window's own panel sound — the two "go -- together"), and you can sell/deposit from the open bag. Homed here in benilla's panel-glue -- file (rather than the bag's own, as in the real client) so every window that opens can call -- them regardless of FrameXML load order — the windows are looked up by name. The real fn -- tracks `backpackWasOpen` so a bag you already had open is LEFT open on the window's close; -- benilla stores that on each frame (`wasOpen`). benilla DIVERGES from the ref here on -- purpose: the real OpenBackpack touches only the backpack, but ours opens EVERY equipped -- bag with the window (director's call — decision 0561 — matching the 'B' all-bags toggle), -- so the names keep the ref's caller contract while the body loops the five windows. The -- list is inlined (like CloseAllWindows above) and every step is guarded, so a surface -- without the bag file — a headless panel test — no-ops rather than erroring. function OpenBackpack() local bags = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4" } for bagId = 0, 4 do -- The backpack (bag 0) always exists; an equipped-bag window only when a bag is in -- the slot (the same existence test as BagFrame.xml's BenillaOpenAllBags). local exists = bagId == 0 or (C_Container and C_Container.GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0) local bag = exists and getglobal(bags[bagId + 1]) if bag then if bag:IsShown() then bag.wasOpen = 1 -- already open: leave it, and don't close it on window hide else bag.wasOpen = nil BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(bag) bag:Show() -- OnShow → igBackPackOpen end end end end
function CloseBackpack() local bags = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4" } for _, name in ipairs(bags) do local bag = getglobal(name) if bag and bag:IsShown() and not bag.wasOpen then bag:Hide() -- OnHide → igBackPackClose end end end
-- BenillaOnEscape() — the ESC keybinding action, run by the host (crates/benilla ui_input) -- when no EditBox consumed the ESCAPE key. The real client binds ESCAPE → TOGGLEGAMEMENU → -- ToggleGameMenu() (UIParent.lua l.1465-1497); its no-menu branch is an if/elseif chain -- (l.1482-1496) that tries, in order: -- if ( StaticPopup_EscapePressed() ) then -- elseif ( OptionsFrame:IsVisible() ) then OptionsFrameCancel:Click() -- elseif ( GameMenuFrame:IsVisible() ) then PlaySound("igMainMenuQuit"); HideUIPanel(GameMenuFrame) -- elseif ( CloseMenus() ) then -- elseif ( SpellStopCasting() ) then -- elseif ( SpellStopTargeting() ) then -- elseif ( CloseAllWindows() ) then -- l.1491 -- elseif ( ClearTarget() ) then -- else PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen"); ShowUIPanel(GameMenuFrame) -- l.1494-1495 -- benilla has no options / game menu / spell targeting yet, so those branches are -- absent and the chain collapses to StaticPopup → CloseMenus → SpellStopCasting → -- CloseAllWindows → ClearTarget, with no menu to open when nothing ate the press. The -- ORDER is the law -- (the director's two-press report, decision 0449): ESC mid-cast cancels the cast and -- ONLY the cast; the target drops on a later press once nothing else claims it. -- ONE benilla addition, ahead of the close: a held cursor item is dropped (ClearCursor). The -- cursor-item model (decision 0068 T2) has no real-client ESC handling to mirror — vanilla -- leaves the item on the cursor — so this is a deliberate benilla convenience (ESC as the -- universal "get me out" key). Guarded so it stays inert were the cursor slice ever absent. function BenillaOnEscape() if CursorHasItem and CursorHasItem() then ClearCursor() end -- An open escapable dialog eats the ESC first (the ref's StaticPopup_EscapePressed — -- defined with the popup engine below): OnCancel(data, "clicked") + hide, but ONLY for -- hideOnEscape entries, so e.g. the DEATH release popup ignores ESC like the ref's. if StaticPopup_EscapePressed() then return end -- The stack-split spinner next (decision 0216 §6/slice 2, StackSplit.xml): the real -- client's own StackSplitFrame hooks ESC directly (its OnKeyDown, `enableKeyboard="true"`) -- — this engine has no plain-frame keyboard capture (StackSplit.xml's own header comment), -- so it routes through this shared chain instead. Just hides (StackSplitFrame_OnHide -- clears the owner's hasStackSplit flag) — no accept, matching a real Cancel click. local split = getglobal("BenillaStackSplitFrame") if split and split:IsVisible() then split:Hide() return end -- The fullscreen world map next (the ref's OnKeyDown ESCAPE arm — WorldMapFrame.xml -- l.628; ours routes through this chain since frames get no raw key events). local worldmap = getglobal("WorldMapFrame") if worldmap and worldmap:IsVisible() then worldmap:Hide() return end -- The open-letter toplevel (decision 0544): the ref registers OpenMailFrame in -- UISpecialFrames (UIParent.lua l.46), so ESC closes it BEFORE the mail panel itself — -- routed through this chain since this v1 drops the UISpecialFrames table. Its OnHide -- runs the taken-letter auto-delete + close sound (MailFrame.lua OpenMailFrame_OnHide). local openmail = getglobal("BenillaOpenMailFrame") if openmail and openmail:IsVisible() then HideUIPanel(openmail) return end -- The ref chain's CloseMenus leg (UIParent.lua l.1488, defined with the dropdown -- engine): an open right-click/dropdown menu closes and eats the press — BEFORE the -- cast cancel, so ESC with a menu up spares a running cast, exactly the ref order. -- Guarded like CursorHasItem above: inert when the dropdown slice isn't loaded. if CloseMenus and CloseMenus() then return end -- The ref chain's SpellStopCasting leg (UIParent.lua l.1489): ESC stops the FIRST -- of {running auto-repeat, in-flight cast} and eats the press — windows close on -- the NEXT press, exactly the reference order. A CHANNEL doesn't answer (nil): the -- ref's 0x6e6e80 can't stop one — the vanilla "/stopcasting can't stop a channel" -- quirk (wow-re esc-stopcasting.md, decision 0454) — so mid-channel the press -- falls through. Truthy only when something was actually stopped (the host's -- stoppable mirror), so an idle ESC still falls through to CloseAllWindows. if SpellStopCasting() then return end -- CloseAllWindows eats the press when it closed anything (l.1491); only a press with -- nothing left to close reaches ClearTarget (l.1492) — the ref's last eater, and the -- ONLY route to the target drop: the raw-key Esc clear the app used to run beside -- this chain double-fired on the first press (decision 0449 retires it). if CloseAllWindows() then return end ClearTarget() end
-- ── The shared dialog IS the ref's StaticPopup engine (decision 0308 §3) ───────────────── -- Transcribed from the patch-chain StaticPopup.lua (mpqx extraction, decision 0246): -- the StaticPopupDialogs registry + StaticPopup_Show(which, arg1, arg2) + the OnUpdate -- countdown/StartDelay machinery — the death arc's dialogs exercise nearly all of it, and -- StaticPopup_Show/StaticPopupDialogs are 1.14 addon-API surface (0068). v1 scope: -- · TWO dialog instances (STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS = 2; the ref runs 4) — the deepest -- nesting exercised so far is decline-res re-showing DEATH (Show precedes the click's -- hide, so a free second instance is required). Grow toward 4 when a third coexists. -- · info fields honored: text, button1, button2, DisplayButton2, OnShow(data), -- OnHide(data), OnAccept(data, data2) (truthy return = keep open — RECOVER_CORPSE -- waits for the server, XP_LOSS's first Accept re-asks), OnCancel(data, reason) -- (reason ∈ "clicked"|"timeout"|"override"), OnUpdate(elapsed, dialog), timeout, -- StartDelay, delayText, sound, whileDead, hideOnEscape, cancels. -- · Accepted but v1-inert: exclusive, showAlert (no alert icon/420-width yet), -- interruptCinematic (cinematics are acked instantly — 0196), notClosableByLogout, -- preferredIndex, and the editbox/money variants. -- · text_arg1/2 stash on the DIALOG frame (the ref stashes them on the Text region; -- our regions don't carry Lua fields). -- · GetText("SECONDS"/"MINUTES") localization collapses to English singular/plural. -- · Button widths stay the template's fixed 120 (the ref widens past 120/110 via -- GetTextWidth; the widen law joins when a longer label first needs it). -- · Resize runs per tick while shown, not only on text swaps: GetHeight's measure has a -- frame of latency (the measured-width convention below), so the height self-corrects -- the frame after any text change. STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS = 2 StaticPopupDialogs = {}
local function StaticPopupTimeUnit(n, minutes) if minutes then if n == 1 then return "minute" end return "minutes" end if n == 1 then return "second" end return "seconds" end
function StaticPopup_FindVisible(which) for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and frame.which == which then return frame end end return nil end
-- Ref l.1870-1877 (returns the frame NAME — the ref's contract). function StaticPopup_Visible(which) local frame = StaticPopup_FindVisible(which) if frame then return frame:GetName() end return nil end
function StaticPopup_Hide(which) for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and frame.which == which then frame:Hide() end end end
-- Ref l.1428-1438, the no-editbox/no-money leg only (v1 has neither variant). function StaticPopup_Resize(dialog, which) local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") local button1 = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button1") dialog:SetHeight(16 + text:GetHeight() + 8 + button1:GetHeight() + 16) end
-- Ref l.1441-1700. Returns the dialog, or nil when refused (whileDead gate / no free -- instance) — calling info.OnCancel() on refusal exactly as the ref does. function StaticPopup_Show(which, text_arg1, text_arg2, data) local info = StaticPopupDialogs[which] if not info then return nil end
-- The whileDead gate (ref l.1447-1452). UnitIsDeadOrGhost lands with the death arc's -- ghost predicate — guarded like CursorHasItem in BenillaOnEscape until then. if UnitIsDeadOrGhost and UnitIsDeadOrGhost("player") and not info.whileDead then if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel() end return nil end
-- Showing X hides a visible X.cancels with an "override" cancel (ref l.1470-1485). if info.cancels then local frame = StaticPopup_FindVisible(info.cancels) if frame then frame:Hide() local OnCancel = StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].OnCancel if OnCancel then OnCancel(frame.data, "override") end end end
-- Showing DEATH sweeps every visible non-whileDead dialog (ref l.1501-1512). if which == "DEATH" then for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and not StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].whileDead then frame:Hide() local OnCancel = StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].OnCancel if OnCancel then OnCancel(frame.data, "override") end end end end
-- A visible same-type dialog is overridden in place; else take a free instance -- (ref l.1515-1553). local dialog = StaticPopup_FindVisible(which) if dialog then if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel(dialog.data, "override") end dialog:Hide() end if not dialog then for i = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. i) if not frame:IsShown() then dialog = frame break end end end if not dialog then if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel() end return nil end
-- The text. Countdown/delay dialogs start blank — their OnUpdate writes it -- (ref l.1556-1574's which-list, verbatim). local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") if (which == "DEATH") or (which == "CAMP") or (which == "QUIT") or (which == "DUEL_OUTOFBOUNDS") or (which == "RECOVER_CORPSE") or (which == "RESURRECT") or (which == "RESURRECT_NO_SICKNESS") or (which == "INSTANCE_BOOT") or (which == "CONFIRM_SUMMON") or (which == "AREA_SPIRIT_HEAL") then text:SetText(" ") dialog.text_arg1 = text_arg1 dialog.text_arg2 = text_arg2 else text:SetText(format(info.text, text_arg1, text_arg2)) end
-- The buttons (ref l.1634-1676; fixed 120 widths — header note). Button2 shows only -- when the entry names it AND DisplayButton2 (when present) allows it; a solo button1 -- re-seats centered under the text. local button1 = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button1") local button2 = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button2") if info.button2 and (not info.DisplayButton2 or info.DisplayButton2()) then button1:ClearAllPoints() button2:ClearAllPoints() button1:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", dialog:GetName() .. "Text", "BOTTOM", -6, -8) button2:SetPoint("LEFT", dialog:GetName() .. "Button1", "RIGHT", 13, 0) button2:SetText(info.button2) button2:Show() else button1:ClearAllPoints() button1:SetPoint("TOP", dialog:GetName() .. "Text", "BOTTOM", 0, -8) button2:Hide() end if info.button1 then button1:SetText(info.button1) button1:Show() else button1:Hide() end
-- Misc vars (ref l.1677-1690). `which` is set before Show so OnShow reads it. dialog.which = which dialog.timeleft = info.timeout or 0 dialog.hideOnEscape = info.hideOnEscape dialog.data = data
if info.StartDelay then dialog.startDelay = info.StartDelay() button1:Disable() else dialog.startDelay = nil button1:Enable() end
dialog:Show() StaticPopup_Resize(dialog, which)
if info.sound then PlaySound(info.sound) end return dialog end
-- Ref l.1850-1868: a truthy OnAccept return keeps the dialog open. function StaticPopup_OnClick(dialog, index) local which = dialog.which local info = StaticPopupDialogs[which] if not info then return end local dontHide = nil if index == 1 then if info.OnAccept then dontHide = info.OnAccept(dialog.data, dialog.data2) end else if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel(dialog.data, "clicked") end end if not dontHide and (which == dialog.which) then dialog:Hide() end end
-- Ref l.1832-1848: the open/close pair sounds on EVERY path, then the entry's own hook. function StaticPopup_OnShow() PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen") local info = StaticPopupDialogs[this.which] if info and info.OnShow then info.OnShow(this.data) end end
function StaticPopup_OnHide() PlaySound("igMainMenuClose") local info = StaticPopupDialogs[this.which] if info and info.OnHide then info.OnHide(this.data) end end
-- Ref l.1712-1808: the timeout countdown (expiry → OnCancel "timeout" + hide), the -- per-tick countdown text for the timer dialogs, the StartDelay gate (button1 disabled, -- delayText counts down, then the real text swaps in and the button enables), then the -- entry's own OnUpdate. The INSTANCE_BOOT/CONFIRM_SUMMON special text formats join with -- their dialogs; their which-list slots stay so the gate is the ref's. function StaticPopup_OnUpdate(dialog, elapsed) local info = StaticPopupDialogs[dialog.which] if not info then return end if (dialog.timeleft or 0) > 0 then local which = dialog.which local timeleft = dialog.timeleft - elapsed if timeleft <= 0 then dialog.timeleft = 0 if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel(dialog.data, "timeout") end dialog:Hide() return end dialog.timeleft = timeleft
if (which == "DEATH") or (which == "CAMP") or (which == "QUIT") or (which == "DUEL_OUTOFBOUNDS") or (which == "INSTANCE_BOOT") or (which == "CONFIRM_SUMMON") or (which == "AREA_SPIRIT_HEAL") then local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") timeleft = ceil(timeleft) if timeleft < 60 then text:SetText(format(info.text, timeleft, StaticPopupTimeUnit(timeleft, false))) else local m = ceil(timeleft / 60) text:SetText(format(info.text, m, StaticPopupTimeUnit(m, true))) end end end if dialog.startDelay then local which = dialog.which local timeleft = dialog.startDelay - elapsed if timeleft <= 0 then dialog.startDelay = nil local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") text:SetText(format(info.text, dialog.text_arg1, dialog.text_arg2)) getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button1"):Enable() return end dialog.startDelay = timeleft
if (which == "RECOVER_CORPSE") or (which == "RESURRECT") or (which == "RESURRECT_NO_SICKNESS") then local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. -- ── The shared frame-fade kit — ref UIParent.lua:1103-1219, transcribed VERBATIM (the -- while-index iteration included; tinsert/tDeleteItem spelled as table.insert / the -- remove loop). The ref drives UIFrameFadeUpdate from UIParent's OnUpdate; our driver is -- the BenillaFadeDriver frame below. Callers: the quest detail write-on -- (QuestFrame.xml) fades TextAlphaDependentFrame in over QUESTINFO_FADE_IN. ────────────── FADEFRAMES = {}
function UIFrameFadeRemoveFrame(frame) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do if FADEFRAMES[index] == frame then table.remove(FADEFRAMES, index) else index = index + 1 end end end
function UIFrameFade(frame, fadeInfo) if not fadeInfo.mode then fadeInfo.mode = "IN" end if fadeInfo.mode == "IN" then if not fadeInfo.startAlpha then fadeInfo.startAlpha = 0 end if not fadeInfo.endAlpha then fadeInfo.endAlpha = 1.0 end elseif fadeInfo.mode == "OUT" then if not fadeInfo.startAlpha then fadeInfo.startAlpha = 1.0 end if not fadeInfo.endAlpha then fadeInfo.endAlpha = 0 end end frame:SetAlpha(fadeInfo.startAlpha) frame.fadeInfo = fadeInfo -- Already fading? Leave the running fade alone (the ref's early return). local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do if FADEFRAMES[index] == frame then return end index = index + 1 end frame:Show() table.insert(FADEFRAMES, frame) end
function UIFrameFadeIn(frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) local fadeInfo = {} fadeInfo.mode = "IN" fadeInfo.timeToFade = timeToFade fadeInfo.startAlpha = startAlpha fadeInfo.endAlpha = endAlpha UIFrameFade(frame, fadeInfo) end
function UIFrameFadeOut(frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) local fadeInfo = {} fadeInfo.mode = "OUT" fadeInfo.timeToFade = timeToFade fadeInfo.startAlpha = startAlpha fadeInfo.endAlpha = endAlpha UIFrameFade(frame, fadeInfo) end
function UIFrameFadeUpdate(elapsed) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do local frame = FADEFRAMES[index] local fadeInfo = frame.fadeInfo if not fadeInfo.fadeTimer then fadeInfo.fadeTimer = 0 end fadeInfo.fadeTimer = fadeInfo.fadeTimer + elapsed if fadeInfo.fadeTimer < fadeInfo.timeToFade then if fadeInfo.mode == "IN" then frame:SetAlpha((fadeInfo.fadeTimer / fadeInfo.timeToFade) * (fadeInfo.endAlpha - fadeInfo.startAlpha) + fadeInfo.startAlpha) elseif fadeInfo.mode == "OUT" then frame:SetAlpha(((fadeInfo.timeToFade - fadeInfo.fadeTimer) / fadeInfo.timeToFade) * (fadeInfo.startAlpha - fadeInfo.endAlpha) + fadeInfo.endAlpha) end else frame:SetAlpha(fadeInfo.endAlpha) if fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime and fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime > 0 then fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime = fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime - elapsed else UIFrameFadeRemoveFrame(frame) if fadeInfo.finishedFunc then fadeInfo.finishedFunc(fadeInfo.finishedArg1, fadeInfo.finishedArg2, fadeInfo.finishedArg3, fadeInfo.finishedArg4) fadeInfo.finishedFunc = nil end end end index = index + 1 end end
function UIFrameIsFading(frame) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do if FADEFRAMES[index] == frame then return 1 end index = index + 1 end return nil end

SelectTab swaps the InActive art for the Active art and disables the button (a -- selected tab doesn't re-click); DeselectTab reverses it. Omitted vs ref: the -- isDisabled/SetDisabledTabState arm (no window has a disabled tab yet) and the SelectTab -- tab-tooltip hide (our tabs set no tooltip). First consumer: the merchant's -- Merchant/Buyback pair. function PanelTemplates_SetNumTabs(frame, numTabs) frame.numTabs = numTabs end
function PanelTemplates_SetTab(frame, id) frame.selectedTab = id PanelTemplates_UpdateTabs(frame) end
function PanelTemplates_GetSelectedTab(frame) return frame.selectedTab end
function PanelTemplates_UpdateTabs(frame) if not frame.selectedTab then return end for i = 1, frame.numTabs do local tab = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Tab" .. i) if i == frame.selectedTab then PanelTemplates_SelectTab(tab) else PanelTemplates_DeselectTab(tab) end end end
function PanelTemplates_DeselectTab(tab) local name = tab:GetName() getglobal(name .. "Left"):Show() getglobal(name .. "Middle"):Show() getglobal(name .. "Right"):Show() tab:Enable() getglobal(name .. "LeftDisabled"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "RightDisabled"):Hide() end
function PanelTemplates_SelectTab(tab) local name = tab:GetName() getglobal(name .. "Left"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "Middle"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "Right"):Hide() tab:Disable() getglobal(name .. "LeftDisabled"):Show() getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):Show() getglobal(name .. "RightDisabled"):Show() end
-- The text-fit (ref PanelTemplates_TabResize, UIPanelTemplates.lua l.31-88, the -- padding-only branch the tab template's OnShow uses — TabResize(0) → tab width = -- text + the two 20px end slices; both middle slices stretch to the text; the text box -- itself un-sizes to natural). One deviation: the ref reads the label's laid-out -- GetWidth (its C measure is synchronous); ours reads GetStringWidth — the same number -- once the measure round-trip lands, which is why the caller below re-checks from -- OnUpdate instead of OnShow. function PanelTemplates_TabResize(padding, tab) local name = tab:GetName() local text = getglobal(name .. "Text") local width = text:GetStringWidth() + (padding or 24) text:SetWidth(0) getglobal(name .. "Middle"):SetWidth(width) getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):SetWidth(width) local sideWidths = 2 * getglobal(name .. "Left"):GetWidth() tab:SetWidth(width + sideWidths) end
-- The tab template's per-frame settle: the ref does TabResize(0) + the highlight width -- in OnShow (CharacterFrameTemplates.xml l.77-80), trusting a synchronous text measure. -- Our GetStringWidth has a frame of latency, so the template's OnUpdate calls this until -- the measured width settles (then it's a no-op compare per frame). function BenillaTabButton_OnUpdate(tab) local text = getglobal(tab:GetName() .. "Text") local w = (text and text:GetStringWidth()) or 0 if w <= 0 or tab.benillaFitWidth == w then return end tab.benillaFitWidth = w PanelTemplates_TabResize(0, tab) getglobal(tab:GetName() .. "HighlightTexture"):SetWidth(w + 30) end
